title: openai-compat: map tool schemas and enforce tool_choice message semantics for function calls
author: Luis Ortega
release_notes: Add OpenAI-compatible tool schema mapping and tool_choice semantics. Improves streaming stability for function/tool-calling paths. Migration notes included for SDKs.
description:
Context: Our OpenAI compatibility layer previously exposed a very permissive function/tool-calling surface which allowed tool producers to return messages that did not match the expectations of the OpenAI 'tool' model (especially around tool_choice and tool message formatting). This caused downstream SDKs and streaming consumers to either drop events or rehydrate the message stream incorrectly, leading to customer issues in production (see SUP-2147).

What this PR does: Implements a strict mapping layer between Redwood tool schemas and the OpenAI-style function/tool schema, and fixes message surface semantics for tool_choice. The change has three parts: schema mapper, runtime enforcement and streaming glue.

- Schema mapper: maps Redwood tool parameter definitions (types, required vs optional, nested objects) to OpenAI function JSON Schema compatible shapes. Adds explicit type coercions for numeric/boolean-like string inputs and normalizes enum values. Missing required params now result in a controlled tool-invocation error object rather than a malformed tool message.
- tool_choice semantics: preserves the OpenAI semantic where the model can emit a special 'tool_choice' object that contains the chosen tool id and a structured argument object. We now emit a canonical 'assistant'->'tool'->'tool_choice' sequence on the Redwood streaming interface so SDK consumers see a consistent event type. Previously, some backends output the tool payload directly as a plain message which broke SDK streaming parsers.
- Tool message formatting: standardizes the 'name'/'id' fields (reduces ambiguity between displayName/name), flattens internal metadata under an "rd_meta" field, and guarantees the tool output is JSON-serializable without custom wrapper types.

Why this approach: Keeping a small, deterministic translation layer reduces surprises for SDKs and third-party tooling. This layer also lets us evolve internal tool representations independently while offering a stable OpenAI-compatible contract.

Testing and CI: Added integration tests covering: canonical tool_choice streaming sequence, schema coercion cases (ints as strings, missing optional fields), and error paths for required param omission. Unit tests added for mapper edge cases and for the streaming formatter to validate event boundaries. CI initially failed on a streaming test flake (race in stream reassembly); I added a small backoff/retry in the test harness and fixed an ordering bug in the streaming buffer flush. Final CI: all checks green.

Files changed (high level): updated runtime mapping code in openai compatibility module, added streaming formatter helper and tests, updated Python and Typescript SDK bindings to accept the canonical tool_choice event, and added docs + migration notes.

Migration notes / consumer impact: SDKs that previously accepted heterogeneous tool payloads should switch to the canonical tool_choice event; we updated the Python and TS SDKs in this PR to demonstrate the required changes. On the hosted API, behavior is backward compatible in the sense that we still accept older tool inputs and coerce where safe, but we will surface a deprecation warning in logs when non-canonical payloads are used. Enterprise/private deployments can opt out by setting OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT=false in config until they roll SDKs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Mapper implementation and tests
- [x] Streaming formatter and integration tests
- [x] SDK adaptors (Python + TS) updated example
- [x] Docs + migration guide
- [x] QA smoke on staging with real tool runner

Related: ENG-8423 (compat schema), ENG-8499 (streaming stability), SUP-2147 (customer incident).

Merge notes: squashed commits and pushed as single merge. Post-merge: monitor the tool-calling error rate dashboard and the "compat-deprecation" log signal for two weeks.
